questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that a raw .tf file diff isn't enough for a pull-request reviewer to approve a Terraform change?
options: Terraform files are always binary and cannot be diffed
.tf files never change between pull requests
GitHub cannot render .tf files in a pull-request diff view at all
A small-looking diff can actually mean creating one resource or destroying and recreating a dozen — only terraform plan's output shows which
questions.explain: A one-line change in a for_each map or a single argument can have a dramatically different real-world effect, which only the actual plan output reveals.

questions.q: What does the `on: pull_request` trigger do in the workflow?
options: Only runs the workflow once, when the repository is first created
Requires a human to manually start the job from the Actions tab every time
Fires the job automatically every time a pull request is opened or updated
Only triggers on pushes directly to the main branch
questions.explain: on: pull_request makes the plan run automatically on every PR open or update, with no one needing to remember to trigger it.

questions.q: Why is `continue-on-error: true` added to the Terraform Plan step?
options: It makes terraform plan run twice as fast
It skips running terraform init before the plan
So a failed plan still gets reported in a later step instead of silently stopping the job before anyone sees why
It is required syntax for every GitHub Actions step and has no functional effect
questions.explain: Without continue-on-error, a failed plan step would stop the job immediately, and the failure would never get posted as a PR comment.

questions.q: What does `github.rest.issues.createComment` do inside the actions/github-script step?
options: Posts a comment directly onto the pull request that triggered the workflow, since a PR is a GitHub issue under the hood
Deletes all previous comments on the pull request
Merges the pull request automatically
Creates a brand-new GitHub issue unrelated to the current pull request
questions.explain: A pull request is a GitHub issue under the hood, which is why the issues API's createComment call is what posts the plan output back onto it.

questions.q: Why does the workflow need `permissions: pull-requests: write` set at the top of the file?
options: Without it, the job can still run terraform plan, but it is not allowed to post a comment back onto the pull request
It is required before terraform init will download any providers
It controls which Terraform version the runner installs
It allows the workflow to automatically merge the pull request
questions.explain: The write permission on pull-requests is what authorizes the later github-script step to actually create a comment on the PR.
